facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is solid and fully sourced from filed statements for FY2025 and for the nine months to September 30, 2026, with the quarter taken from the filed statements and the release. On the group's own leverage definition, which divides net debt by last-twelve-months Segment Adjusted EBITDA that excludes non-cash metal price lag, leverage moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x at September 30, 2026 by our calculation, close to the 1.6x the company reports. The improvement came mostly from earnings, not from deleveraging: total debt fell by 127 while earnings excluding metal price lag rose by 345 between FY2025 and the LTM to September 30, 2026. On Adjusted EBITDA as reported, which includes metal price lag, the same ratios are lower (1.23x net at September 30, 2026), so the basis chosen matters and is shown. Cash interest cover, liquidity and the maturity profile are comfortable in the near term, with the main structural facts being fixed-rate unsecured notes that mature mainly in 2029 and 2032, a secured asset-based revolver that is undrawn, and sizable off-balance-sheet receivables factoring. The view is limited because covenant levels, the credit agreement and the indentures are not in the pack, and because Adjusted EBITDA and net debt are management measures.

facts.label: Leverage and coverage reading
facts.text: Risk mechanic: the improvement is mostly numerator-driven. Earnings excluding lag rose by 345 between the FY2025 and LTM windows (720 to 1,065) while net debt fell by 165 (1,824 to 1,659). A leverage ratio that falls on earnings is exposed to a reversal in the earnings drivers: the company attributes the quarter to improved aerospace and transportation conditions, supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America and strong recycling, and the P&ARP segment rose 98% in Q3 on favorable metal costs and price and mix (10-Q Q3 page:24, 36). Treating the factoring programs as debt-like lifts the ratio: total debt plus the 417 derecognized receivables over LTM earnings excluding lag is 2.10x (calculated; not a company or covenant measure).

facts.label: Covenants and definitions
facts.text: The senior note indentures carry incurrence-style limits on debt, restricted payments, liens, asset sales and mergers, and a 101% change-of-control offer (10-K page:35, 108). The only maintenance covenant located is the fixed charge coverage ratio on the Pan-U.S. ABL, tested only if availability falls below 10% of commitments. The company states compliance with all applicable financial debt covenants at March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026 (each quarterly debt note) and at December 31, 2025 and 2024 (10-K page:110). The covenant level, the definition and the reported ratio are Not supplied. Definition differences that matter: Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation, factoring expenses, restructuring, impairment, unrealized derivative gains and losses and non-operating pension items, and includes metal price lag; the company's leverage uses Segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes lag; net debt as defined by the company adjusts for cross-currency basis swaps net of margin calls and for cash pledged for guarantees (Release Q3 page:12); and factoring expense (15 in 9M 2026) sits in other gains and losses, outside finance costs. The metric computed here (carrying-value debt less cash over EBITDA excluding lag) differs from the company's only by the 1 swap adjustment at September 30, 2026.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Constellium SE is the French parent of a global converter of aluminum into rolled and extruded products for aerospace, packaging and automotive customers, organized in three segments. The business model is metal pass-through plus a conversion margin, so long-run credit performance depends on end-market volumes, product mix and plant efficiency rather than on the aluminum price itself, although metal prices drive revenue, working capital and the non-cash metal price lag that sits inside reported Adjusted EBITDA. Revenue is spread across products and regions but the 10 largest customers are a majority of sales, qualification requirements create switching costs that support retention, and contracts in the largest end markets are multi-year. There is no transaction under review in the context: the recent corporate actions are a partial redemption of the 2028 notes, share repurchases under a renewed program, a cancellation of treasury shares, a small disposal of a joint venture interest, a plan settlement in the US pension and an amendment of the US asset-based facility after quarter-end. Ownership, control rights, guarantor perimeter and distribution capacity are not documented in the pages supplied, so governance conclusions are limited to documented actions and sponsor behavior is not assessed.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The context supplies no transaction: deal terms, sponsor, borrower and parent are blank, so there is no transaction to analyze and no sponsor behavior to assess. The record of capital structure events in the supplied sources is as follows. In August 2024 the company issued dollar and euro senior notes due 2032 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the remaining 2026 dollar and euro notes, which left no senior notes maturing before 2028 (completed; 10-K page:65, 109). In July 2026 it redeemed part of the 5.625% notes due 2028, leaving a smaller outstanding amount (completed within Q3 2026; 10-Q Q3 page:15). No new debt issue occurred in Q3 2026 in the pages read, and the debt table shows no new instrument. On October 22, 2026, after the quarter-end and within the cutoff, the US asset-based facility was amended to raise commitments and extend maturity (a subsequent event, described in CP-1; 10-Q Q3 page:23); the 10-Q lists the amending agreement as Amendment No. 8 filed as Exhibit 10.1 (10-Q Q3 page:43), so the document exists but is not in the pack, and its terms beyond commitment size and maturity are Not supplied. This refines the earlier readiness note, which described the amendment document as not supplied; that remains true of the pack. On shareholder returns, a new repurchase program of up to 300 was authorized on March 12, 2026, effective May 21, 2026 and expiring December 31, 2028, replacing the previous program; about 257 remained at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:43). The board approved cancellation of 6 million treasury shares on September 17, 2026, with no cash effect (10-Q Q3 page:13). A 54% interest in Changchun Engley Automobile Parts Co. LTD was disposed of on June 24, 2026 for net cash of 2 (10-Q Q3 page:23). In Q3 2026 the group also settled the Ravenswood Salaried Pension Plan through lump-sum payments and an annuity purchase, derecognizing 47 of obligations and 44 of assets (10-Q Q3 page:20). Credit effect: these actions reduce interest-bearing debt modestly and the amendment raises facility commitments, but they leave the 2029 and 2032 maturities unchanged (see CP-1); the use of cash for repurchases competes with further debt reduction.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: the 10 largest customers are approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue and contracts in the largest end markets are multi-year with rigorous qualification (10-K page:13, 7, 8). Risk mechanic: qualification and switching costs support retention and volume visibility, but concentration means a loss or repricing at one account moves volumes and margin materially; general industrial contracts are one year or less. Credit implication: revenue visibility supports debt service in the near term, while a downturn in packaging or automotive volumes would weaken coverage; the concentration risk factor is stated by the company (10-K page:30). Counter-evidence: the cover-page error-correction mark versus the immaterial revision narrative (see Conflicts) does not bear on revenue but bears on the reliability of segment earnings.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: metal price lag was 222 of 1,074 of 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, and inventories rose to 1,905 from 1,407 (CP-1; 10-Q Q3 page:4, 41). Risk mechanic: in rising metal prices reported earnings include non-cash lag while inventories and receivables absorb cash; a price decline reverses the lag. Credit implication: leverage and coverage should be read on the basis excluding lag, and free cash flow of 223 in 9M 2026 can fall short of earnings in a price spike.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: the largest segment supplies 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings; the top 10 metal suppliers are approximately 49% of purchases by volume (10-K page:53, 12). Risk mechanic: dependence on two concentrated sides, customers and metal suppliers, with internal casthouses partly mitigating supply. Credit implication: an operational disruption at a key rolling site (the 2024 Valais flood is an example of site-level loss) can affect a large share of earnings; insurance proceeds offset part of that loss (10-K page:68, 61).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Constellium SE has a sound fundamental credit profile, with moderate and falling leverage, adequate liquidity and no senior notes maturing before 2028. Net debt was USD 1,659 million, or 1.56x Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag, at September 30, 2026, against 2.53x at FY2025, and total liquidity was USD 992 million. The strongest support is qualification-protected, mostly multi-year customer relationships in aerospace, packaging and automotive. The weakest point is earnings quality: 20.7% of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported was non-cash metal price lag, and management links part of the uplift to supply shortages. What decides the outcome is whether margins hold as metal prices and those shortages normalize, and how the USD 841 million of 2029 notes is refinanced.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage has fallen mainly because earnings rose, not because debt shrank (Documentary Fact from the financial base, with an Analyst Interpretation). Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and total debt to the same measure from 2.70x to 1.71x. Earnings excluding lag rose by USD 345 million between those windows while total debt fell by USD 127 million. A ratio that falls on the numerator reverses if the earnings drivers reverse, so Constellium SE carries leverage that sits inside its 1.5x to 2.5x target range but has little demonstrated durability. Treating USD 417 million of receivables derecognized under factoring as debt-like lifts total debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag to 2.10x, an analyst sensitivity rather than a company measure.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Debt service is comfortable at current earnings (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag covered cash interest paid 10.65x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 6.92x for FY2025, and the senior notes carry fixed coupons, so rate moves do not change cash interest on the notes. The cover is earnings-dependent and shares the earnings quality caveat above.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings quality is the central analytical issue (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Metal price lag was USD 222 million of USD 1,074 million of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, 20.7%, and it turned negative at USD 4 million in Q3 2026 when aluminum prices fell. Revenue rose 26% in the nine months on higher revenue per ton while shipments were down 1%. In a rising price phase, inventories (USD 1,905 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 1,407 million at December 31, 2025) and receivables absorb cash, which is why nine-month 2026 working capital lines were an outflow of USD 488 million even as free cash flow of USD 223 million exceeded the USD 68 million of the prior-year nine months. Management attributes part of Q3 2026 to supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America; that is Management Language and cannot be assumed to persist.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate in the near term and the facility profile improved after quarter-end (Documentary Fact). Total liquidity of USD 992 million comprises USD 158 million of cash, USD 541 million of asset-based facility availability, USD 114 million of French facility availability and USD 179 million of factoring availability. Cash plus committed undrawn facilities is USD 813 million. The asset-based facility is undrawn and was amended on October 22, 2026 to raise commitments from USD 550 million to USD 700 million and extend maturity to October 22, 2031 (subsequent event; effect on availability not disclosed). The French facility, which matures in December 2027 per the annual report, is the nearest facility maturity.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The maturity wall is concentrated in 2029 and 2032 (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on refinancing cost). Face value of USD 225 million falls due in 2028, USD 841 million in 2029 (46.4% of USD 1,812 million total face value) and USD 691 million in 2032 (38.1%). The 2029 notes carry coupons of 3.750% and 3.125%, against 6.375% and 5.375% on the 2024 issues, so refinancing the 2029 notes at coupons like the 2024 issues would raise annual interest cost. The USD 100 million partial redemption of the 2028 notes in July 2026 shows a willingness to retire debt early when notes are callable at par.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Business risk rests on qualification-based relationships and is offset by concentration (Documentary Fact). Packaging and automotive rolled products supply 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings; the 10 largest customers are approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue; contracts in aerospace, packaging and automotive are mostly multi-year while general industrial contracts are one year or less. Metal cost is largely passed through, so margin risk sits in conversion margin, volumes and mix; the group has single-site loss precedent in the 2024 Valais flood.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Capital allocation is mixed (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on direction). Nine-month 2026 share repurchases of USD 78 million were alongside the partial note redemption; a new repurchase program of up to USD 300 million was authorized in March 2026 with about USD 257 million remaining, and no dividend is intended. Leverage inside the target range gives management room to continue returning cash, which competes with further debt reduction. Whether the indentures restrict that capacity cannot be tested.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Customer relationships protected by qualification (Documentary Fact): switching costs and mostly multi-year contracts in the largest end markets support volume visibility and retention. Leverage and coverage (Documentary Fact): net leverage of 1.56x and cash interest cover of 10.65x leave debt service comfortable at current earnings, and a cushion against a moderate earnings decline. Liquidity and maturity runway (Documentary Fact): USD 992 million of total liquidity, an undrawn asset-based facility with a longer tenor after the October 2026 amendment, and no senior notes maturing before 2028 give time to manage a downturn. Fixed-rate funding (Documentary Fact): fixed coupons on the senior notes limit cash interest sensitivity to rates. Diversified end markets and footprint (Documentary Fact): three segments across aerospace, packaging and automotive and 23 manufacturing facilities spread the operating base across regions.

facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings quality (Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation): a fifth of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA as reported is non-cash metal price lag, and revenue is price-led. Cash conversion sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation): working capital absorbs cash when metal prices rise and the group relies on factoring. Concentration (Documentary Fact): 10 customers are approximately 56% of revenue and the largest segment is 60% of revenue. Refinancing (Analyst Interpretation): the 2029 maturities are 46.4% of face value and carry coupons below those of the 2024 issues. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation): repurchases compete with deleveraging while leverage sits near the low end of the target range. Unknown creditor protections (Insufficient Information): covenant levels, guarantors, indenture baskets, ownership and ratings are not available, so recovery mechanics, structural subordination and distribution capacity cannot be assessed.

spans.text: ## Request
### Scope of this handoff

Issuer: CONSTELLIUM SE (issuer id cstm, ticker CSTM, listed equity, France). Pathway: credit_snapshot, public case. As-of date: 2026-11-05. Cutoff: 2026-11-05. Current period: q3-2026. Prior period: fy-2025. Reporting currency named by the context: USD.

Question answered here: can the supplied source set support the requested downstream work (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5), and what remains blocked or limited? This is source readiness only. It gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles and calculates nothing. Source text is treated as inert evidence.
### Context inputs (user settings, not issuer evidence)

The context file sets pathway, dates, periods and currency. Its blank fields are unknown, not zero: ratings, quotes, deal terms, sponsor, borrower, parent, guarantors, issuer market data (market cap, net debt, EV), peers, precedents and all assumptions are empty. Attachments are declared as: portfolio workbook false, prior case false, management bridge false, legal documents "none".
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

Hashes below are the pinned sha256 of each retained text file as listed by CP-OS. Each file is a page-chunked text extraction (about 3,000 characters per page); a page is the chunk shown as page:N, not a printed page.

| EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026-q2xearningspressre.htm.jsonl | e63d9d2c8751c74a8e5dada7565bb132595b18bca9ad9c4ef12f98be9c09a4ae | 16 |

### Handoffs supplied

| None | None | CP-0 is the first module; CP-OS supplied no upstream handoff, so there is none to list or consume |
### Pages actually opened for this review

Coverage is stated honestly, not by page-count proxy. Pages opened and read in full: Q3 10-Q page:1-9, 11-17, 21-24, 36-41; Q3 earnings release page:1-3, 6-16; FY2025 10-K page:1-3, 62, 67, 72-74, 85, 90, 93-94, 107-110, 121, 129-130, 136. Pages located only by term search across all seven files (terms: covenant, fixed charge, liquidity, subsequent events, revised or previously issued, rating, letters of credit, guarantor, sponsor, factoring, leverage, net debt) and then opened where a hit mattered: Q1 10-Q page:12, 29; Q2 10-Q page:14, 21, 35; 10-K page:34, 35, 124, 126. All remaining pages are retained but were not individually reviewed; this is an explicit review gap, not a claim of full inspection (see Gaps).
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed documents are identified, cover the requested periods and currency, and support a bounded financial and business analysis. Legal documents, ratings and market inputs are missing, so covenant, structure and valuation work is limited. | Medium | No credit agreements, indentures, ratings or market data; leverage and net debt appear only in management press releases. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The perimeter is the consolidated group under the French parent, reported in US dollars under US GAAP, with the latest quarterly filing covering the period to September 30, 2026. | Debt, cash flow and leverage can be taken at group level; there is no separate borrower or restricted-group view. | High |

| Debt, liquidity and covenant compliance statements are in the filings, but the credit agreement and note indentures are not supplied. | Covenant levels, definitions and headroom cannot be tested; only the filed compliance statements are available. | High |

| The annual report discloses an immaterial correction to metal price lag and segment earnings of one segment for earlier periods. | Earlier-period segment comparisons need the revised figures and a caution about metal price lag. | Medium |

| Net debt and leverage appear in the earnings releases but not in the quarterly filing. | These management measures cannot be confirmed against a filing and carry a lower evidential weight. | Medium |

| A revolving facility amendment dated after quarter-end is described only briefly, with no amendment document. | New commitment size and maturity rest on a one-sentence disclosure; terms are unverified. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient for the requested snapshot, with limitations, and nothing is blocked outright. The three quarterly filings, the annual report and the three earnings releases identify the same registrant, the same reporting currency and consecutive periods, so identity and perimeter are resolved for the consolidated group. The set is not sufficient for legal-document-dependent work: no credit agreement, indenture, amendment or waiver was supplied, so covenant definitions, baskets and the terms of the post-quarter facility amendment cannot be verified, and no rating, quote, peer or market input exists. Source sufficiency here does not mean the downstream analysis is complete, and the CP-MODEL input contract is not evaluated (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED).
### Source-by-source assessment
| Source | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Evidence located (quote) |

| Earnings release Q1 2026 | Management press release furnished as exhibit; attributed supporting claims, not controlling over filings | Constellium SE group | Quarter ended March 31, 2026; includes non-GAAP measures | “first quarter ended March 31, 2026” (page:1) |

Roles named in the sources: issuer and registrant Constellium SE (France); the senior notes are “senior unsecured obligations of Constellium SE” guaranteed by certain subsidiaries (10-K page:108); the Pan-U.S. ABL borrowers are Ravenswood, Muscle Shoals and Bowling Green (10-K page:108); the French Inventory Facility borrowers are Constellium Issoire S.A.S. and Constellium Neuf-Brisach S.A.S. | Liquidity | Total liquidity with components at each quarter end | “At September 30, 2026, we had $992 million of total liquidity” (10-Q Q3 page:38); “At December 31, 2025, we had $866 million of total liquidity” (10-K page:62) |

| Covenants | Compliance statements each period; one named maintenance covenant on the Pan-U.S. ABL with a springing trigger | “The Group was in compliance with all applicable financial debt covenants at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025.” (10-Q Q3 page:15); “Evaluation of compliance with the maintenance covenant is only required if the borrowing availability falls below 10% of the aggregate revolving loan commitments.” (10-K page:108) |

| Management measures | Net debt, leverage and free cash flow definitions and values | “Leverage is defined as Net debt divided by last twelve months Segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes the non-cash impact of metal price lag.” (Earnings release Q3 page:12) |
### Version relationships and duplicates

The three earnings releases and three quarterly reports are separate active sources for different periods; none supersedes another. Each earnings release repeats figures that also appear in the same-period quarterly filing; for example the Q3 release carries “Revenue 2,639 2,166 7,848 6,248” (Earnings release Q3 page:12) and the Q3 10-Q carries “Revenue 2 2,639 2,166 7,848 6,248” with a note column (10-Q Q3 page:3). No duplicate files were found: all seven sha256 values differ, and the visible-text hash printed in each file header differs from the pinned file hash, so the pinned hash is used as the source identity here.

### Scope

Issuer: CONSTELLIUM SE (cstm), the consolidated group (Constellium SE and its subsidiaries), as of 2026-11-05 with cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Current period: Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026), with nine months 2026 and last twelve months (LTM) to September 30, 2026 where a flow is needed against a balance. Prior period: FY2025. Reporting currency and unit: US dollars, millions (US$m), US GAAP, as the context names and the filings print.

Task: extract the reported financial base, compute leverage, coverage, liquidity and maturity data with every formula shown, review definitions, and state what the evidence supports. This is a financial base handoff. It is not a credit rating view.
### Period labels used

FY2025 is the year ended December 31, 2025 (audited annual report). Q3 2026 is the three months ended September 30, 2026. 9M 2026 and 9M 2025 are the nine months ended September 30. LTM Q3 2026 is calculated as FY2025 plus 9M 2026 minus 9M 2025 for every flow; balances are at the dates stated. No other period is mixed into a sentence without a label.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

### Financial base view

The financial base is solid and fully sourced from filed statements for FY2025 and for the nine months to September 30, 2026, with the quarter taken from the filed statements and the release. On the group's own leverage definition, which divides net debt by last-twelve-months Segment Adjusted EBITDA that excludes non-cash metal price lag, leverage moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x at September 30, 2026 by our calculation, close to the 1.6x the company reports. The improvement came mostly from earnings, not from deleveraging: total debt fell by 127 while earnings excluding metal price lag rose by 345 between FY2025 and the LTM to September 30, 2026. On Adjusted EBITDA as reported, which includes metal price lag, the same ratios are lower (1.23x net at September 30, 2026), so the basis chosen matters and is shown. Cash interest cover, liquidity and the maturity profile are comfortable in the near term, with the main structural facts being fixed-rate unsecured notes that mature mainly in 2029 and 2032, a secured asset-based revolver that is undrawn, and sizable off-balance-sheet receivables factoring. The view is limited because covenant levels, the credit agreement and the indentures are not in the pack, and because Adjusted EBITDA and net debt are management measures.

### Leverage and coverage reading

Evidence: net debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag moved from 2.53x (FY2025) to 1.56x (LTM Q3 2026), and total debt to the same measure from 2.70x to 1.71x. The company reports 2.2x at March 31, 2026, 1.8x at June 30, 2026 and 1.6x at September 30, 2026 (Release Q1, Q2 and Q3 page:1).

Risk mechanic: the improvement is mostly numerator-driven. Earnings excluding lag rose by 345 between the FY2025 and LTM windows (720 to 1,065) while net debt fell by 165 (1,824 to 1,659). A leverage ratio that falls on earnings is exposed to a reversal in the earnings drivers: the company attributes the quarter to improved aerospace and transportation conditions, supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America and strong recycling, and the P&ARP segment rose 98% in Q3 on favorable metal costs and price and mix (10-Q Q3 page:24, 36). Treating the factoring programs as debt-like lifts the ratio: total debt plus the 417 derecognized receivables over LTM earnings excluding lag is 2.10x (calculated; not a company or covenant measure).

Credit implication: leverage sits inside management's stated 1.5x to 2.5x target range at the low end (Release Q3 page:2), so there is limited room to reduce further by design; the company is also returning cash to shareholders (78 of repurchases in 9M 2026 against free cash flow of 223) rather than only repaying debt. Cash interest cover of 10.65x is comfortable. Covenant headroom cannot be assessed because levels are not supplied.
### Cash flow quality

Evidence: cash from operations was 420 in 9M 2026 against 271 in 9M 2025, but inventories absorbed 527 and receivables 267, partly offset by payables of 310 (10-Q Q3 page:5), and the company ascribes the movements to higher metal prices and activity (10-Q Q3 page:39). The working capital lines sum to an outflow of 488 in 9M 2026 against 161 in 9M 2025 (calculated).

Risk mechanic (analyst interpretation): when aluminum prices rise, metal price lag adds to reported earnings (non-cash, 222 in 9M 2026) while inventory and receivables absorb cash. The lag turned negative in Q3 2026 (-4), which the company ties to primary aluminum prices decreasing (Release Q3 page:6). Metal price lag was 21% of 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported (222 of 1,074, calculated), so in a rising price phase reported Adjusted EBITDA runs ahead of cash earnings.

Credit implication: free cash flow of 223 in 9M 2026 (68 in 9M 2025) is reported cash. The 2026 guidance of free cash flow above 300 needs more than 77 in the fourth quarter (300 less 223, calculated), against Q3 free cash flow of 128; the guidance is management's, not a filed fact. Cash conversion remains dependent on metal price direction and on factoring programs continuing, since 417 of receivables are sold.
### Liquidity

Total liquidity was 992 at September 30, 2026: cash 158, Pan-U.S. ABL availability 541, factoring availability 179 and French facility availability 114 (sum 992). Excluding factoring, cash plus committed undrawn facilities was 813 (158 + 655, calculated). No margin calls were reported at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:38). Both facilities were undrawn at September 30, 2026. Pan-U.S. ABL availability of 541 against commitments of 550 is far above the 10% trigger for the fixed charge coverage test (55 on the 550 of commitments, calculated), so on the face of the figures the test would not be required; the borrowing availability definition is not supplied, so this is indicative only. The French facility matures in December 2027 per the annual report (10-K page:108; not restated in the 10-Q), about 13 months after the cutoff, and is the nearest facility maturity. The October 22, 2026 amendment of the ABL increases commitments from 550 to 700 and extends maturity to October 22, 2031 (10-Q Q3 page:23); the effect on availability is not disclosed.
### Covenants and definitions

The senior note indentures carry incurrence-style limits on debt, restricted payments, liens, asset sales and mergers, and a 101% change-of-control offer (10-K page:35, 108). The only maintenance covenant located is the fixed charge coverage ratio on the Pan-U.S. ABL, tested only if availability falls below 10% of commitments. The company states compliance with all applicable financial debt covenants at March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026 (each quarterly debt note) and at December 31, 2025 and 2024 (10-K page:110). The covenant level, the definition and the reported ratio are Not supplied. Definition differences that matter: Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation, factoring expenses, restructuring, impairment, unrealized derivative gains and losses and non-operating pension items, and includes metal price lag; the company's leverage uses Segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes lag; net debt as defined by the company adjusts for cross-currency basis swaps net of margin calls and for cash pledged for guarantees (Release Q3 page:12); and factoring expense (15 in 9M 2026) sits in other gains and losses, outside finance costs. The metric computed here (carrying-value debt less cash over EBITDA excluding lag) differs from the company's only by the 1 swap adjustment at September 30, 2026.

### Subsequent events and quarter events to the cutoff

On July 28, 2026 the company redeemed 100 of the 325 outstanding 5.625% notes due 2028, leaving 225 (10-Q Q3 page:15; Release Q3 page:7). This is inside Q3 2026. On September 17, 2026 the board approved cancellation of 6 million treasury shares, which reduced issued shares and has no cash effect (10-Q Q3 page:13). On June 24, 2026 the group disposed of its 54% interest in Changchun Engley Automobile Parts Co. LTD for a net cash inflow of 2 (10-Q Q3 page:23). After the quarter, on October 22, 2026, the Pan-U.S. ABL was amended (commitments 550 to 700, maturity to October 22, 2031); it is a subsequent event within the cutoff and its terms beyond those two items are Not supplied. Guidance raised on October 28, 2026: Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag 1.03 billion to 1.06 billion and free cash flow above 300 for 2026 (Release Q3 page:8); management guidance, not a filed fact. Implied fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag is 178 to 208 (guidance range less 852 for 9M 2026, calculated).
### Readiness for downstream use

The pack supports a bounded financial base. Restricted conclusions: covenant headroom (levels and definitions Not supplied), guarantor perimeter and subsidiary-level structural subordination (guarantor list not supplied), the effect of the October 22, 2026 ABL amendment on availability, and any rating or market-based view (no ratings or prices supplied). Where the CP-0 handoff placed limits on these items they are carried unchanged.
## Calculations
All inputs are US$m from the cited locators. LTM = FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025.
### LTM flows

Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. This handoff is business and transaction context. It gives no rating, recovery conclusion, peer ranking or instrument recommendation.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Constellium is a scaled maker of rolled and extruded aluminum products with diversified end markets, qualification-based customer relationships and mostly multi-year contracts. Customer concentration, metal price exposure and unknown ownership are the main uncertainties. | Medium | Ownership detail sits in an unsupplied proxy statement, and no indentures or credit agreements were provided, so control, guarantor and distribution-capacity questions stay open. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Packaging and automotive rolled products supply 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings, ahead of aerospace and transportation and automotive structures. | Earnings lean on can, beverage and automotive demand; a volume shortfall in the largest segment weighs most on the group. | Medium |

| The 10 largest customers represent approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue, with multi-year contracts in the largest end markets. | Qualification and contracts support revenue visibility, but losing or repricing one large customer would hit volumes and margins. | High |

| Prices pass through aluminum cost, so revenue, working capital and reported earnings move with metal prices; metal price lag is non-cash. | Reported earnings can run ahead of cash earnings when prices rise, and working capital then absorbs cash. | Medium |

| Shareholder returns come through buybacks, with a new program authorized in March 2026 and no dividend intended; debt was partly redeemed in July 2026. | Mixed signal: some deleveraging, while cash also goes to equity. Distribution capacity under the indentures cannot be tested. | Medium |
| Ownership and control are not disclosed in the supplied pages, and no sponsor or controlling holder is named. | Control and support behavior cannot be judged; treat as unknown, not adverse. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

Constellium SE is the French parent of a global converter of aluminum into rolled and extruded products for aerospace, packaging and automotive customers, organized in three segments. The business model is metal pass-through plus a conversion margin, so long-run credit performance depends on end-market volumes, product mix and plant efficiency rather than on the aluminum price itself, although metal prices drive revenue, working capital and the non-cash metal price lag that sits inside reported Adjusted EBITDA. Revenue is spread across products and regions but the 10 largest customers are a majority of sales, qualification requirements create switching costs that support retention, and contracts in the largest end markets are multi-year. There is no transaction under review in the context: the recent corporate actions are a partial redemption of the 2028 notes, share repurchases under a renewed program, a cancellation of treasury shares, a small disposal of a joint venture interest, a plan settlement in the US pension and an amendment of the US asset-based facility after quarter-end. Ownership, control rights, guarantor perimeter and distribution capacity are not documented in the pages supplied, so governance conclusions are limited to documented actions and sponsor behavior is not assessed.

| Area | Fact | Category | Credit translation | Source |

| Revenue mix | FY2025 revenue of 8,449 by segment before eliminations: Packaging & Automotive Rolled Products (P&ARP) 60%, Aerospace & Transportation (A&T) 23%, Automotive Structures & Industry (AS&I) 19%. Segment share of FY2025 Segment Adjusted EBITDA: P&ARP 49%, A&T 47%, AS&I 10%, Holdings & Corporate -6%. | Documentary Fact | Revenue and earnings are weighted differently: A&T is a smaller revenue block but nearly as large an earnings block as P&ARP, which points to higher conversion margins in aerospace (analyst interpretation). Loss of volume in P&ARP matters most for scale. | 10-K page:53 |

| Pricing | Products are priced on the LME price, a regional premium and a conversion margin; the model aims to pass metal cost through and hedge any remaining exposure. | Documentary Fact; the neutrality aim is Management Language | Metal price is largely a pass-through, so margin risk sits in conversion margin, volumes and mix; revenue and receivables scale with metal price. | 10-K page:55, 5 |

| Metal price lag | Metal price lag is a non-cash timing effect between sales and purchase prices of metal and is included in Adjusted EBITDA as reported: 126 in FY2025 and 222 in 9M 2026, negative 4 in Q3 2026. | Documentary Fact | Earnings quality: part of reported Adjusted EBITDA is not cash; leverage should be read on the basis excluding lag (see CP-1: net 1.56x on that basis at September 30, 2026, 1.23x on Adjusted EBITDA as reported). | 10-K page:67; 10-Q Q3 page:41 |

| Tariffs and premiums | The average Midwest premium was 1,298 per ton in FY2025 against 432 in FY2024, and the all-in US aluminum price rose 38%. | Documentary Fact | US metal cost inflation raises working capital needs and inflates revenue; tariff policy remains an uncertainty the company itself flags. | 10-K page:55, 24 |

| Customers | The 10 largest customers represent approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue; relationships often span decades; qualification is rigorous and creates high switching costs. | Documentary Fact; the switching-cost description is Management Language | Concentration is material, offset by stickiness; a single large program loss or repricing would be visible in volumes. | 10-K page:13, 30 |

| Contract tenor | Largest aerospace contracts are mostly multi-year; commercial transportation and defense are one to three years; general industrial one year or less; packaging and automotive contracts are typically multi-year, and automotive structures contracts usually last the life of a model. | Documentary Fact | Revenue visibility is strongest in aerospace, packaging and automotive programs and weakest in general industrial. | 10-K page:7, 8 |

| Suppliers and inputs | The top 10 metal suppliers are approximately 49% of metal purchases by volume; most slab and billet needs come from internal casthouses; energy is one of the largest operating costs after metal, labor and depreciation. | Documentary Fact | Supply concentration and energy cost are operating risks; internal casthouses reduce external dependency and support recycling margins. | 10-K page:12, 31 |

| Volume drivers | Shipments were 1,120 thousand metric tons in 9M 2026 against 1,130 in 9M 2025 (down 1%); the 26% revenue rise in 9M 2026 came from higher revenue per ton, including metal prices. | Documentary Fact | Revenue growth is price-led, not volume-led, so revenue growth overstates operating growth. | Release Q3 page:3 |

| Seasonality | Lowest volumes are typically delivered in August and December and highest from January to July; can demand is strongest in spring and summer and automotive and aerospace slow in the third and fourth quarters. | Documentary Fact | Quarterly cash flow is uneven; the third and fourth quarters are structurally weaker for volumes. | 10-K page:13 |

| Cost structure | Cost of sales excluding depreciation and amortization was 86% of FY2025 revenue; the group employs approximately 11,500 people, about 50% of US employees and a majority of non-US employees under collective bargaining agreements. | Documentary Fact | Analyst interpretation: because metal is passed through, cost of sales moves with revenue, while labor under collective agreements is a less flexible cost. | 10-K page:56, 15 |

| Capital spending | Net capital expenditure was 311 in FY2025 and 197 in 9M 2026 (CP-1), described as relating primarily to maintenance and investments in manufacturing facilities. | Documentary Fact; the maintenance-and-investment description is Management Language | Capex runs near the level of depreciation (330 in FY2025), so free cash flow depends on holding spend discipline. | 10-Q Q3 page:39; 10-K page:77 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The context supplies no transaction: deal terms, sponsor, borrower and parent are blank, so there is no transaction to analyze and no sponsor behavior to assess. The record of capital structure events in the supplied sources is as follows. In August 2024 the company issued dollar and euro senior notes due 2032 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the remaining 2026 dollar and euro notes, which left no senior notes maturing before 2028 (completed; 10-K page:65, 109). In July 2026 it redeemed part of the 5.625% notes due 2028, leaving a smaller outstanding amount (completed within Q3 2026; 10-Q Q3 page:15). No new debt issue occurred in Q3 2026 in the pages read, and the debt table shows no new instrument. On October 22, 2026, after the quarter-end and within the cutoff, the US asset-based facility was amended to raise commitments and extend maturity (a subsequent event, described in CP-1; 10-Q Q3 page:23); the 10-Q lists the amending agreement as Amendment No. 8 filed as Exhibit 10.1 (10-Q Q3 page:43), so the document exists but is not in the pack, and its terms beyond commitment size and maturity are Not supplied. This refines the earlier readiness note, which described the amendment document as not supplied; that remains true of the pack. On shareholder returns, a new repurchase program of up to 300 was authorized on March 12, 2026, effective May 21, 2026 and expiring December 31, 2028, replacing the previous program; about 257 remained at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:43). The board approved cancellation of 6 million treasury shares on September 17, 2026, with no cash effect (10-Q Q3 page:13). A 54% interest in Changchun Engley Automobile Parts Co. LTD was disposed of on June 24, 2026 for net cash of 2 (10-Q Q3 page:23). In Q3 2026 the group also settled the Ravenswood Salaried Pension Plan through lump-sum payments and an annuity purchase, derecognizing 47 of obligations and 44 of assets (10-Q Q3 page:20). ### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: the 10 largest customers are approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue and contracts in the largest end markets are multi-year with rigorous qualification (10-K page:13, 7, 8). Risk mechanic: qualification and switching costs support retention and volume visibility, but concentration means a loss or repricing at one account moves volumes and margin materially; general industrial contracts are one year or less. Credit implication: revenue visibility supports debt service in the near term, while a downturn in packaging or automotive volumes would weaken coverage; the concentration risk factor is stated by the company (10-K page:30). Counter-evidence: the cover-page error-correction mark versus the immaterial revision narrative (see Conflicts) does not bear on revenue but bears on the reliability of segment earnings.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: metal price lag was 222 of 1,074 of 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, and inventories rose to 1,905 from 1,407 (CP-1; 10-Q Q3 page:4, 41). Risk mechanic: in rising metal prices reported earnings include non-cash lag while inventories and receivables absorb cash; a price decline reverses the lag. Credit implication: leverage and coverage should be read on the basis excluding lag, and free cash flow of 223 in 9M 2026 can fall short of earnings in a price spike.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: the largest segment supplies 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings; the top 10 metal suppliers are approximately 49% of purchases by volume (10-K page:53, 12). Risk mechanic: dependence on two concentrated sides, customers and metal suppliers, with internal casthouses partly mitigating supply. Credit implication: an operational disruption at a key rolling site (the 2024 Valais flood is an example of site-level loss) can affect a large share of earnings; insurance proceeds offset part of that loss (10-K page:68, 61).

4. Sponsor and ownership alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named; the proxy statement is not supplied (10-K page:126, 128). Risk mechanic: without ownership data, willingness to support or extract cannot be judged. Credit implication: Insufficient Information; this is a monitoring item, not an adverse conclusion. Documented actions point to a mixed capital allocation policy: partial debt redemption alongside repurchases.

5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: indentures, credit agreements and the guarantor list are not in the pack (CP-0). Risk mechanic: covenant headroom, restricted payment capacity and the guarantor perimeter drive creditor protection and structural subordination. Credit implication: these limit any conclusion on recovery prospects or priority; recovery prospects can appear only as a mechanic, and no expected recovery outcome is given.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Constellium SE has a sound fundamental credit profile: net leverage fell to 1.56x with USD 992 million of liquidity and no senior notes due before 2028. Earnings quality and the 2029 refinancing, not near-term liquidity, decide the outcome. | Medium | Covenant levels, indentures, guarantors, ownership and ratings are not in the sources, so creditor protection and distribution capacity are unassessed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag fell from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x at September 30, 2026, driven mainly by higher earnings. | Leverage sits inside the 1.5x to 2.5x target range but depends on earnings that could reverse. | Medium |

| Metal price lag was 20.7% of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, and revenue growth was price-led rather than volume-led. | Earnings quality is lower than reported figures suggest; read leverage on the basis excluding lag. | Medium |

| Liquidity is USD 992 million, of which USD 179 million is factoring availability; the asset-based facility was upsized after quarter-end. | Committed liquidity is the cleaner downside measure; factoring access is less certain in stress. | Medium |

| USD 841 million of notes mature in 2029 and USD 691 million in 2032, at coupons below those of the 2024 issues. | Refinancing the 2029 notes at higher coupons would raise interest cost; this is the key medium-term event. | Medium |
| Ownership, covenant levels, guarantors and indenture baskets are not available. | Creditor protection cannot be tested; this is unknown, not adverse. | Not assessable |
### Credit view

Constellium SE has a sound fundamental credit profile, with moderate and falling leverage, adequate liquidity and no senior notes maturing before 2028. Net debt was USD 1,659 million, or 1.56x Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag, at September 30, 2026, against 2.53x at FY2025, and total liquidity was USD 992 million. The strongest support is qualification-protected, mostly multi-year customer relationships in aerospace, packaging and automotive. The weakest point is earnings quality: 20.7% of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported was non-cash metal price lag, and management links part of the uplift to supply shortages. What decides the outcome is whether margins hold as metal prices and those shortages normalize, and how the USD 841 million of 2029 notes is refinanced.
### Key findings

Leverage has fallen mainly because earnings rose, not because debt shrank (Documentary Fact from the financial base, with an Analyst Interpretation). Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and total debt to the same measure from 2.70x to 1.71x. Earnings excluding lag rose by USD 345 million between those windows while total debt fell by USD 127 million. A ratio that falls on the numerator reverses if the earnings drivers reverse, so Constellium SE carries leverage that sits inside its 1.5x to 2.5x target range but has little demonstrated durability. Treating USD 417 million of receivables derecognized under factoring as debt-like lifts total debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag to 2.10x, an analyst sensitivity rather than a company measure.

Debt service is comfortable at current earnings (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag covered cash interest paid 10.65x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 6.92x for FY2025, and the senior notes carry fixed coupons, so rate moves do not change cash interest on the notes. The cover is earnings-dependent and shares the earnings quality caveat above.

Earnings quality is the central analytical issue (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Metal price lag was USD 222 million of USD 1,074 million of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, 20.7%, and it turned negative at USD 4 million in Q3 2026 when aluminum prices fell. Revenue rose 26% in the nine months on higher revenue per ton while shipments were down 1%. In a rising price phase, inventories (USD 1,905 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 1,407 million at December 31, 2025) and receivables absorb cash, which is why nine-month 2026 working capital lines were an outflow of USD 488 million even as free cash flow of USD 223 million exceeded the USD 68 million of the prior-year nine months. Management attributes part of Q3 2026 to supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America; that is Management Language and cannot be assumed to persist.

Liquidity is adequate in the near term and the facility profile improved after quarter-end (Documentary Fact). Total liquidity of USD 992 million comprises USD 158 million of cash, USD 541 million of asset-based facility availability, USD 114 million of French facility availability and USD 179 million of factoring availability. Cash plus committed undrawn facilities is USD 813 million. The asset-based facility is undrawn and was amended on October 22, 2026 to raise commitments from USD 550 million to USD 700 million and extend maturity to October 22, 2031 (subsequent event; effect on availability not disclosed). The French facility, which matures in December 2027 per the annual report, is the nearest facility maturity.

The maturity wall is concentrated in 2029 and 2032 (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on refinancing cost). Face value of USD 225 million falls due in 2028, USD 841 million in 2029 (46.4% of USD 1,812 million total face value) and USD 691 million in 2032 (38.1%). The 2029 notes carry coupons of 3.750% and 3.125%, against 6.375% and 5.375% on the 2024 issues, so refinancing the 2029 notes at coupons like the 2024 issues would raise annual interest cost. The USD 100 million partial redemption of the 2028 notes in July 2026 shows a willingness to retire debt early when notes are callable at par.

Business risk rests on qualification-based relationships and is offset by concentration (Documentary Fact). Packaging and automotive rolled products supply 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings; the 10 largest customers are approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue; contracts in aerospace, packaging and automotive are mostly multi-year while general industrial contracts are one year or less. Metal cost is largely passed through, so margin risk sits in conversion margin, volumes and mix; the group has single-site loss precedent in the 2024 Valais flood.

Capital allocation is mixed (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on direction). Nine-month 2026 share repurchases of USD 78 million were alongside the partial note redemption; a new repurchase program of up to USD 300 million was authorized in March 2026 with about USD 257 million remaining, and no dividend is intended. Leverage inside the target range gives management room to continue returning cash, which competes with further debt reduction. Whether the indentures restrict that capacity cannot be tested.

Claims outside the debt figure add to the creditor burden (Documentary Fact). Pension and other benefit obligations were USD 341 million on the balance sheet at September 30, 2026, close-down and environmental provisions were USD 86 million, and the group is party to factoring programs under which USD 417 million of receivables were derecognized. None of these is in the USD 1,817 million of total debt.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Customer relationships protected by qualification (Documentary Fact): switching costs and mostly multi-year contracts in the largest end markets support volume visibility and retention. Leverage and coverage (Documentary Fact): net leverage of 1.56x and cash interest cover of 10.65x leave debt service comfortable at current earnings, and a cushion against a moderate earnings decline. Liquidity and maturity runway (Documentary Fact): USD 992 million of total liquidity, an undrawn asset-based facility with a longer tenor after the October 2026 amendment, and no senior notes maturing before 2028 give time to manage a downturn. Fixed-rate funding (Documentary Fact): fixed coupons on the senior notes limit cash interest sensitivity to rates. Diversified end markets and footprint (Documentary Fact): three segments across aerospace, packaging and automotive and 23 manufacturing facilities spread the operating base across regions.

Weaknesses. Earnings quality (Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation): a fifth of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA as reported is non-cash metal price lag, and revenue is price-led. Cash conversion sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation): working capital absorbs cash when metal prices rise and the group relies on factoring. Concentration (Documentary Fact): 10 customers are approximately 56% of revenue and the largest segment is 60% of revenue. Refinancing (Analyst Interpretation): the 2029 maturities are 46.4% of face value and carry coupons below those of the 2024 issues. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation): repurchases compete with deleveraging while leverage sits near the low end of the target range. Unknown creditor protections (Insufficient Information): covenant levels, guarantors, indenture baskets, ownership and ratings are not available, so recovery mechanics, structural subordination and distribution capacity cannot be assessed.
### Fundamental credit assessment

| Thesis | Constellium SE is a qualification-protected aluminum converter whose improved leverage rests on strong but partly price-driven earnings, so the credit holds if margins persist and the 2029 notes are refinanced without a sharp cost increase | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same as above |

| Confidence limit | Confidence is below High because legal documents, ownership and ratings are not supplied and CP-1A rated its own gap on the legal documents as High severity | Insufficient Information | Not applicable | CP-1A gaps ledger |
### Key credit risks

| Earnings quality: metal price lag and price-led revenue | Rising aluminum prices add non-cash lag to reported earnings and absorb cash in inventory and receivables; falling prices reverse the lag | Reported Adjusted EBITDA overstates cash earnings in a price spike; leverage read on reported earnings is understated | Material | CP-1 leverage and cash flow quality; CP-1A metal price lag row |

| Working capital and factoring dependence | USD 417 million of receivables are sold and USD 179 million of liquidity is factoring availability; inventories absorbed USD 527 million of cash in nine months of 2026 | Loss of factoring capacity or a metal price rise draws on committed liquidity of USD 813 million | Material | CP-1 liquidity and cash flow quality |

| Unknown creditor protections | Indentures, credit agreements, guarantor list and ownership are not supplied | Structural subordination, covenant headroom and distribution capacity cannot be tested | Material | CP-0 limits; CP-1A gaps |

| Shareholder distributions versus deleveraging | A new repurchase program of up to USD 300 million with about USD 257 million remaining | Leverage could stop falling or rise if cash is directed to equity; baskets are unknown | Minor | CP-1A governance and transaction rows |

| Trade policy and US metal premiums | The average Midwest premium was USD 1,298 per ton in FY2025 against USD 432 in FY2024, and tariffs remain uncertain | Cost and working capital swings in the US business; tariff changes could shift demand | Minor | CP-1A operating model row |

| Obligations outside debt | Pension and other benefit obligations of USD 341 million and close-down and environmental provisions of USD 86 million | Cash calls on top of debt service in a stress | Minor | CP-1 claims outside debt table |
